bug_semantics: On Linux/Unix, an attacker-controlled RAR entry such as `..\..\tmp\evil.txt` is first checked as a child of the extraction directory while backslashes are literal filename characters, so `getCanonicalPath().startsWith(destination.getCanonicalPath())` accepts it. `makeFile()` then splits that same name on backslashes, joins the components with the platform `File.separator` (`/`), creates the resulting directories/file, and `extract()` writes attacker-controlled entry bytes through `FileOutputStream`. The validation and the write therefore interpret the same pathname differently, enabling traversal and arbitrary file overwrite outside the destination. Windows is not affected by this bypass because canonicalization already treats backslashes as separators.
flaw_origin: The earliest public Git commit, root commit 6f32323c983015d96c64084418793853f514b519 (`initial import`), first writes the operative vulnerable extraction logic in `testutil/src/main/java/de/innosystec/unrar/testutil/ExtractArchive.java`: it splits entry names on backslashes, rebuilds them with `File.separator`, and opens the result for output. Subsequent commits only relocate or copy that logic: 7e0c503f3afe6da766e4476333bc3ee9cd677bb1 renames the package, e5b90d174c5a426a134b00a33ddece3ac9e82a39 moves it into the main unrar module, bb362df3e1e5471e58f6322c91b7b1c9a8ebaef1 moves the module tree, 75cb6a58c9b3ca08db954eec241b91a5331dd632 copies it into `Junrar`, and 3b645d991563dd8933f6efab135cd76a43a92d6b copies it into `LocalFolderExtractor`. Commit e60b915f8932c08b9b6874a97f00676decba069a later added canonical-path validation but left the backslash-to-platform-separator conversion after the check, so it failed to close the original Unix traversal.

evidence: Bundle GHSA-j273-m5qq-6825/CVE-2026-28208 identifies `com.github.junrar:junrar < 7.5.8`, first patched 7.5.8, and directly references fix 947ff1d33f00f940aa68ae2593500291d799d954. In the assigned clone, reproduce the origin with `git log --all --reverse -S'name.split("\\\\")' -- .`: the first hit is root 6f32323c983015d96c64084418793853f514b519; later hits are copies/moves and the fix. `git show 6f32323c983015d96c64084418793853f514b519:testutil/src/main/java/de/innosystec/unrar/testutil/ExtractArchive.java` shows `name.split("\\\\")`, accumulation with `File.separator`, `createNewFile()`, and writing via `FileOutputStream`. `git rev-list --parents -n 1 6f32323c983015d96c64084418793853f514b519` prints only that SHA, directly proving there is no parent; the vulnerable code is therefore absent from the empty parent state. Follow the copies with `git log --follow -- testutil/src/main/java/de/innosystec/unrar/testutil/ExtractArchive.java`, then its renamed paths, and `git log -L 57,94:src/main/java/com/github/junrar/LocalFolderExtractor.java c7041fc07df2cc397ea46ba516933ee9725af250`; the latter traces the unchanged split/rebuild logic and the 2019 canonical check. `git show 947ff1d33f00f940aa68ae2593500291d799d954 -- src/main/java/com/github/junrar/LocalFolderExtractor.java` shows the closing change: normalize `fh.getFileName()` with `path.replace("\\", "/")` before constructing/canonicalizing `File`, then split the normalized name on `/`. `git rev-parse v7.5.7^{} v7.5.8^{}` yields 04481cf28bb121b976077b3ab7d7e1adec82687f and 97bf405418d0997717d55e0556045ff80945e099; `git show v7.5.7:src/main/java/com/github/junrar/LocalFolderExtractor.java` has raw-name canonicalization followed by backslash splitting, while the v7.5.8 blob has normalization before validation. `git tag --contains 947ff1d33f00f940aa68ae2593500291d799d954 --sort=version:refname` begins at v7.5.8, confirming the release boundary. Finally, `git cat-file -p 6f32323c983015d96c64084418793853f514b519` reproduces the BIC-only marker check and its absence.
reasoning: The security defect predates the later validation: the root commit already made archive-controlled `..` components actionable by translating backslash-delimited names into host separators before writing. The 2018 relocations are not BICs, and the 2019 canonical-path check is an incomplete attempted mitigation rather than the first vulnerable implementation. The direct 2026 fix aligns validation and write interpretation by normalizing separators before canonicalization and is first released in v7.5.8. AI attribution is judged only from the true BIC commit object; that 2010 human-authored root object contains no AI attribution trailer or bot identity, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
